A 1x non-participating preference at most: money back first, or a share of the sale, not both.
Wickhatch stays Apache-2.0; no term may require closing it or relicensing it.

explain.plain: With a participating preference, Kestrel Row takes its £1.2m back first and then also takes its percentage of what is left. It is paid twice from the same sale. A non-participating preference gives the investor the larger of the two, not both.
example: Kestrel Row would own 20.0% under v1. A sale at £10,000,000:
Participating (v1): £1,200,000 + 20.0% × £8,800,000 = £2,960,000 to Kestrel Row; Ana Brindle gets £6,195,200.
Non-participating (v4 style): the larger of £1,200,000 and 20.0% × £10,000,000 = £2,000,000; Ana Brindle gets £7,040,000.
A sale at £3,000,000: participating gives Kestrel Row £1,560,000 and Ana Brindle £1,267,200; non-participating gives Kestrel Row £1,200,000 and Ana Brindle £1,584,000.

explain.plain: If a later round sells shares cheaper, a full ratchet reprices all of Kestrel Row's shares to the new low price, however little is raised at it. The founder and staff pay for the difference. A weighted average adjusts in proportion to how much is raised at the lower price.
example: Suppose a later round raises £800,000 at £3.20 a share (down from £4.80), issuing 250,000 shares.
Full ratchet: Kestrel Row's 250,000 shares become £1,200,000 ÷ £3.20 = 375,000, an extra 125,000. Ana Brindle falls to 54.2%.
Broad-based weighted average: new price = £4.80 × (1,250,000 + 166,667) ÷ (1,250,000 + 250,000) = £4.53; Kestrel Row holds 264,706, an extra 14,706. Ana Brindle falls to 58.1%.

explain.plain: A drag-along lets the holders who approve a sale force every other shareholder to sell on the same terms. Under v1 the trigger is 50% of the preferred shares, and Kestrel Row would hold all of them: Kestrel Row alone could sell the company.
example: Under v1 Kestrel Row holds 250,000 of 250,000 preferred shares: 100% of the class, so it meets the 50% trigger alone, while owning 20.0% of the company.
A £3,000,000 offer forced through under v1 terms would pay Kestrel Row £1,560,000 and Ana Brindle £1,267,200, though Ana Brindle owns 70.4%.
Under v4 a drag needs the board and holders of 60% of all shares; Ana Brindle holds 67.7%, so no sale is forced without Ana Brindle.
explain.agreed: v4: the board plus 60% of all shares; and the exit clause if control is lost.

explain.plain: Re-vesting means shares the founder already owns become "unvested" again and are earned back month by month. If the founder leaves early, the unearned part can be bought back cheaply. It ties the founder to the company.
example: v1: all 880,000 shares re-vest over 48 months. If Ana Brindle left after 12 months, 660,000 would be unvested: £3,168,000 at the round price, bought back at nominal value.
v4: 25% of 775,834 = 193,959 shares re-vest over 24 months. After 12 months, 96,980 would be unvested: £465,504 at the round price, and only a bad leaver loses them at nominal value.

explain.plain: Consent matters are decisions the company cannot take without the investor's written yes. A long list means the investor can slow or block ordinary running of the company, and under v1 it covered the licence of Wickhatch.
example: Illustration: Brindlewood expects about 14 decisions a year that would hit a v1 consent matter (a hire above £90,000, a contract above £100,000, a budget change).
If each consent takes 6 working days, that is 84 working days of waiting a year under v1.
Under v4: 9 matters, about 5 such decisions a year, deemed consent after 5 working days: no more than 25 working days, and never on the licence.
explain.agreed: v4: 9 consent matters, none touching the open-source licence (u3).

content.text: On a Liquidation Event the holders of Preferred Shares shall first receive an amount equal to 1x the Subscription Price and shall thereafter participate pro rata with the holders of Ordinary Shares in the balance.

content.text: The Board shall comprise three Directors: the Founder, one Director appointed by the Investor, and one independent Director appointed with the Investor's prior written approval.

content.title: Investor consent matters
content.text: The Company shall not, without Investor Consent, do any of the 18 matters in Schedule 2, including any change to the licence terms of any software owned by the Company.

content.title: Information rights
content.text: The Company shall deliver to the Investor monthly management accounts within 20 Business Days of each month end, and an annual budget.

content.title: Drag-along
content.text: If holders of 50 per cent of the Preferred Shares approve a Sale, all Shareholders shall transfer their Shares on the same terms.

content.title: Subscription
content.text: On Completion the Investor shall subscribe for 125,000 Series Seed Preferred Shares at £4.80 per share, a subscription price of £600,000, payable in cleared funds to the Company.

content.title: Purchase of existing shares
content.text: On Completion the Founder shall sell and the Investor shall buy 125,000 Ordinary Shares held by the Founder at £4.80 per share, a price of £600,000, free of encumbrances.

content.title: Founder loan
content.text: Within 10 Business Days of Completion the Founder shall lend the Company £400,000 on the terms of the Loan Note in Schedule 4.

content.title: Liquidation preference
content.text: On a Liquidation Event each holder of Preferred Shares shall receive the greater of (a) 1x the Subscription Price and (b) the amount it would receive had its Preferred Shares converted to Ordinary Shares, and not both.

content.title: Board composition
content.text: The Board shall comprise three Directors: the Founder, one Director appointed by the Investor, and one independent Director appointed by the Founder. The Founder shall chair the Board with a casting vote.

content.title: Founder exit right
content.text: If at any time the Founder ceases to be able to appoint or control a majority of the Board, the Founder may, by notice given within 24 months, require the Investor to buy, or procure a buyer for, all of the Founder's Shares at the price per share of the latest equity round.

content.title: Investor consent matters
content.text: The Company shall not, without Investor Consent, do any of the 7 matters in Schedule 2. Consent is deemed given if not refused within 5 Business Days. No matter in Schedule 2 extends to the licence of Wickhatch.

content.title: Open-source licence
content.text: Wickhatch shall remain licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. No provision of this Agreement or of the Articles shall require the Company to close, withdraw or relicense Wickhatch.

content.title: Warranties
content.text: The Founder and the Company warrant to the Investor in the terms of Schedule 3, and the Investor warrants to the Company and the Founder in the terms of Schedule 3A (standing, authority, funds and conflicts).

content.title: Limit on liability
content.text: The aggregate liability of the Founder under the Warranties and any indemnity shall not exceed the amount invested by the Investor, and the aggregate liability of the Investor under Schedule 3A shall be capped on the same basis.

content.title: Anti-dilution
content.text: If the Company issues New Securities at a price per share below the Subscription Price, the conversion price of each Preferred Share shall be adjusted on a broad-based weighted average basis, as set out in Article 9.

content.title: Founder re-vesting
content.text: 15 per cent of the Founder's Shares shall re-vest monthly over 12 months from Completion; if the Founder leaves as a Bad Leaver, unvested shares may be bought back at nominal value, and on any other departure at market value.

content.title: Information rights
content.text: The Company shall deliver to the Investor monthly management accounts within 20 Business Days of each month end. The Investor shall report to the Company each quarter on the standing of the Fund, its conflicts and any holding in a competitor of the Company.

content.title: Drag-along
content.text: If the Board and holders of 75 per cent of all Shares approve a Sale, all Shareholders shall transfer their Shares on the same terms.

content.title: Plain-language precedence
content.text: Each clause has a plain-language projection in English and in Portuguese, signed with this Agreement. Where a clause and its plain-language projection differ, the projection states the intent of the parties and the clause shall be read to give effect to it.

content.title: Signed understandings
content.text: Each Understanding signed by counsel for both parties binds the drafting of this Agreement. A clause that contradicts a signed Understanding is void until both parties sign it again.

why.t-amount: Sell, don't issue: £600,000 of the round buys existing founder shares, so fewer new shares dilute the company.
why.t-loan: Ana Brindle lends £400,000 of the sale proceeds back, so the company still receives £1,000,000 of working money.
why.t-preference: Simple preference: money back or a share of the sale, not both.
why.t-board: Control: the founder keeps a majority on the board.
why.t-consents: Control and open source: fewer consent matters, deemed consent, licence outside every matter.
why.t-exit: Exit clause: if the founder loses control, the founder may sell at the round price, within 24 months.
why.t-indemnity: Mirror: warranties both ways; cap at the amount invested, for both sides.
why.t-antidilution: Full ratchet replaced with the market-standard weighted average.
why.t-revesting: Ana Brindle has built the company for a year; the founder desk offers 15% over one year.
why.t-drag: Control: a sale needs the board and 75% of all shares, not 50% of one class.
why.t-plain: Plain terms: every clause gets a signed plain projection.
why.t-understandings: No surprises: signed understandings bind the drafting.

content.title: Subscription
content.text: On Completion the Investor shall subscribe for 166,666 Series Seed Preferred Shares at £4.80 per share, a subscription price of £799,996.80, payable in cleared funds to the Company.

content.title: Purchase of existing shares
content.text: On Completion the Founder shall sell and the Investor shall buy 83,333 Ordinary Shares held by the Founder at £4.80 per share, a price of £399,998.40, free of encumbrances.

content.title: Founder loan
content.text: Within 10 Business Days of Completion the Founder shall lend the Company £200,000, unsecured and free of interest, repayable on completion of the Company's next priced equity round, on the terms of the Loan Note in Schedule 4.

content.title: Liquidation preference
content.text: On a Liquidation Event the holders of Preferred Shares shall first receive an amount equal to 1x the Subscription Price and shall thereafter participate pro rata with the holders of Ordinary Shares in the balance, provided that the total received by each holder shall not exceed 3x its Subscription Price.

content.title: Board composition
content.text: The Board shall comprise three Directors: the Founder, one Director appointed by the Investor, and one independent Director appointed by the Founder from three candidates approved in advance by the Investor, such approval not to be unreasonably withheld.

content.title: Founder exit right
content.text: If at any time the Founder ceases to be able to appoint or control a majority of the Board, the Founder may, by notice given within 6 months, require the Investor to buy, or procure a buyer for, all of the Founder's Shares at the price per share of the latest equity round.

content.title: Investor consent matters
content.text: The Company shall not, without Investor Consent, do any of the 11 matters in Schedule 2. Consent is deemed given if not refused within 5 Business Days. No matter in Schedule 2 extends to the licence of Wickhatch.

content.title: Open-source licence
content.text: Wickhatch shall remain licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. No provision of this Agreement or of the Articles shall require the Company to close, withdraw or relicense Wickhatch.

content.title: Warranties
content.text: The Founder and the Company warrant to the Investor in the terms of Schedule 3, and the Investor warrants to the Company and the Founder in the terms of Schedule 3A (standing, authority, funds and conflicts). Claims under the intellectual property and tax warranties may be brought within 3 years of Completion.

content.title: Limit on liability
content.text: The aggregate liability of the Founder under the Warranties and any indemnity shall not exceed twice the amount invested by the Investor, and the aggregate liability of the Investor under Schedule 3A shall be capped on the same basis.

content.title: Anti-dilution
content.text: If the Company issues New Securities at a price per share below the Subscription Price, the conversion price of each Preferred Share shall be adjusted on a broad-based weighted average basis, as set out in Article 9.

content.title: Founder re-vesting
content.text: 50 per cent of the Founder's Shares shall re-vest monthly over 36 months from Completion; if the Founder leaves as a Bad Leaver, unvested shares may be bought back at nominal value, and on any other departure at market value.

content.title: Information rights
content.text: The Company shall deliver to the Investor monthly management accounts within 20 Business Days of each month end. The Investor shall report to the Company each year on the standing of the Fund and its conflicts, and within 10 Business Days of acquiring any holding in a competitor of the Company.

content.title: Drag-along
content.text: If the Board and holders of 60 per cent of all Shares approve a Sale, all Shareholders shall transfer their Shares on the same terms, subject to Article 4.

content.title: Plain-language precedence
content.text: Each clause has a plain-language projection in English and in Portuguese, signed with this Agreement. Where a clause and its plain-language projection differ, the projection states the intent of the parties and the clause shall be read to give effect to it.

content.title: Signed understandings
content.text: Each Understanding signed by counsel for both parties binds the drafting of this Agreement. A clause that contradicts a signed Understanding is void until both parties sign it again.

payload.plain: With a participating preference, Kestrel Row takes its £1.2m back first and then also takes its percentage of what is left. It is paid twice from the same sale. A non-participating preference gives the investor the larger of the two, not both.
example: Kestrel Row would own 20.0% under v1. A sale at £10,000,000:
Participating (v1): £1,200,000 + 20.0% × £8,800,000 = £2,960,000 to Kestrel Row; Ana Brindle gets £6,195,200.
Non-participating (v4 style): the larger of £1,200,000 and 20.0% × £10,000,000 = £2,000,000; Ana Brindle gets £7,040,000.
A sale at £3,000,000: participating gives Kestrel Row £1,560,000 and Ana Brindle £1,267,200; non-participating gives Kestrel Row £1,200,000 and Ana Brindle £1,584,000.

payload.plain: If a later round sells shares cheaper, a full ratchet reprices all of Kestrel Row's shares to the new low price, however little is raised at it. The founder and staff pay for the difference. A weighted average adjusts in proportion to how much is raised at the lower price.
example: Suppose a later round raises £800,000 at £3.20 a share (down from £4.80), issuing 250,000 shares.
Full ratchet: Kestrel Row's 250,000 shares become £1,200,000 ÷ £3.20 = 375,000, an extra 125,000. Ana Brindle falls to 54.2%.
Broad-based weighted average: new price = £4.80 × (1,250,000 + 166,667) ÷ (1,250,000 + 250,000) = £4.53; Kestrel Row holds 264,706, an extra 14,706. Ana Brindle falls to 58.1%.

payload.plain: A drag-along lets the holders who approve a sale force every other shareholder to sell on the same terms. Under v1 the trigger is 50% of the preferred shares, and Kestrel Row would hold all of them: Kestrel Row alone could sell the company.
example: Under v1 Kestrel Row holds 250,000 of 250,000 preferred shares: 100% of the class, so it meets the 50% trigger alone, while owning 20.0% of the company.
A £3,000,000 offer forced through under v1 terms would pay Kestrel Row £1,560,000 and Ana Brindle £1,267,200, though Ana Brindle owns 70.4%.
Under v4 a drag needs the board and holders of 60% of all shares; Ana Brindle holds 67.7%, so no sale is forced without Ana Brindle.

payload.plain: Re-vesting means shares the founder already owns become "unvested" again and are earned back month by month. If the founder leaves early, the unearned part can be bought back cheaply. It ties the founder to the company.
example: v1: all 880,000 shares re-vest over 48 months. If Ana Brindle left after 12 months, 660,000 would be unvested: £3,168,000 at the round price, bought back at nominal value.
v4: 25% of 775,834 = 193,959 shares re-vest over 24 months. After 12 months, 96,980 would be unvested: £465,504 at the round price, and only a bad leaver loses them at nominal value.

payload.plain: Consent matters are decisions the company cannot take without the investor's written yes. A long list means the investor can slow or block ordinary running of the company, and under v1 it covered the licence of Wickhatch.
example: Illustration: Brindlewood expects about 14 decisions a year that would hit a v1 consent matter (a hire above £90,000, a contract above £100,000, a budget change).
If each consent takes 6 working days, that is 84 working days of waiting a year under v1.
Under v4: 9 matters, about 5 such decisions a year, deemed consent after 5 working days: no more than 25 working days, and never on the licence.

Version v3 of the Brindlewood Security seed term sheet, as sent. Signed by the investor desk agents as proof of authorship; counsel sign-off blocked by the consistency check.
We sign the agreed text v4 of the Brindlewood Security seed round.

payload.en: Kestrel Row puts £699,998.40 into the company for 145,833 new preferred shares at £4.80 each.
payload.pt: A Kestrel Row investe £699.998,40 na empresa e recebe 145.833 novas ações preferenciais a £4,80 cada.
payload.note: Plain English and plain Portuguese (Portugal). Where they differ from the clause, the plain version states the intent.

payload.en: Kestrel Row also buys 104,166 of Ana Brindle's existing shares at the same £4.80 each, paying Ana Brindle £499,996.80.
payload.pt: A Kestrel Row compra também 104.166 ações existentes de Ana Brindle ao mesmo preço de £4,80 cada, pagando £499.996,80 a Ana Brindle.
payload.note: Plain English and plain Portuguese (Portugal). Where they differ from the clause, the plain version states the intent.

payload.en: Ana Brindle lends £300,000 of that money to the company, with no interest, to be repaid when the company next raises a priced round.
payload.pt: Ana Brindle empresta £300.000 desse valor à empresa, sem juros, a reembolsar quando a empresa fizer a próxima ronda de investimento com preço.
payload.note: Plain English and plain Portuguese (Portugal). Where they differ from the clause, the plain version states the intent.

payload.en: If the company is sold, Kestrel Row gets its money back first or its share of the sale, whichever is more, never both.
payload.pt: Se a empresa for vendida, a Kestrel Row recebe primeiro o dinheiro que investiu ou a sua parte da venda, o que for maior, nunca as duas coisas.
payload.note: Plain English and plain Portuguese (Portugal). Where they differ from the clause, the plain version states the intent.

payload.en: The board has three people: Ana Brindle, a Kestrel Row director, and an independent that Ana Brindle chooses from three names Kestrel Row has approved.
payload.pt: O conselho de administração tem três pessoas: Ana Brindle, um administrador da Kestrel Row e um administrador independente escolhido por Ana Brindle entre três nomes aprovados pela Kestrel Row.
payload.note: Plain English and plain Portuguese (Portugal). Where they differ from the clause, the plain version states the intent.

payload.en: If Ana Brindle loses control of the board, Ana Brindle can sell all of Ana Brindle's shares at the last round's price within 12 months: the exit is when you sell control.
payload.pt: Se Ana Brindle perder o controlo do conselho, pode vender todas as suas ações ao preço da última ronda, no prazo de 12 meses: a saída acontece quando se vende o controlo.
payload.note: Plain English and plain Portuguese (Portugal). Where they differ from the clause, the plain version states the intent.

payload.en: Nine big decisions, such as issuing new shares or selling the company, need Kestrel Row's consent; five working days of silence counts as yes; Wickhatch's licence is never one of them.
payload.pt: Nove decisões importantes, como emitir novas ações ou vender a empresa, precisam do consentimento da Kestrel Row; cinco dias úteis de silêncio contam como sim; a licença do Wickhatch nunca é uma delas.
payload.note: Plain English and plain Portuguese (Portugal). Where they differ from the clause, the plain version states the intent.

payload.en: Wickhatch stays Apache-2.0 for good; nothing in the deal can force it closed or relicensed.
payload.pt: O Wickhatch mantém a licença Apache-2.0 para sempre; nada no acordo pode obrigar a fechá-lo ou a mudar a sua licença.
payload.note: Plain English and plain Portuguese (Portugal). Where they differ from the clause, the plain version states the intent.

payload.en: Both sides make promises: Brindlewood and Ana Brindle about the company, Kestrel Row about its own standing and money. Claims can be made for two years, three for tax.
payload.pt: Ambos os lados dão garantias: a Brindlewood e Ana Brindle sobre a empresa, a Kestrel Row sobre a sua própria situação e os seus fundos. As reclamações podem ser feitas durante dois anos, três no caso dos impostos.
payload.note: Plain English and plain Portuguese (Portugal). Where they differ from the clause, the plain version states the intent.

payload.en: If a promise turns out wrong, Ana Brindle's total liability is capped at the amount Kestrel Row invested, £1,200,000; Kestrel Row's is capped the same way.
payload.pt: Se uma garantia se revelar falsa, a responsabilidade total de Ana Brindle tem como limite o montante investido pela Kestrel Row, £1.200.000; a da Kestrel Row tem o mesmo limite.
payload.note: Plain English and plain Portuguese (Portugal). Where they differ from the clause, the plain version states the intent.

payload.en: If a later round is priced lower, Kestrel Row gets a partial top-up of shares, weighted by how much was raised at the lower price, not a full reset.
payload.pt: Se uma ronda posterior tiver um preço mais baixo, a Kestrel Row recebe uma compensação parcial em ações, ponderada pelo montante angariado a esse preço, e não uma reposição total.
payload.note: Plain English and plain Portuguese (Portugal). Where they differ from the clause, the plain version states the intent.

payload.en: A quarter of Ana Brindle's shares are earned back over two years; if Ana Brindle leaves early as a bad leaver, the part not yet earned can be bought back at nominal value, otherwise at market value.
payload.pt: Um quarto das ações de Ana Brindle volta a ser adquirido ao longo de dois anos; se Ana Brindle sair cedo como 'bad leaver', a parte ainda não adquirida pode ser recomprada ao valor nominal, nos outros casos ao valor de mercado.
payload.note: Plain English and plain Portuguese (Portugal). Where they differ from the clause, the plain version states the intent.

payload.en: Brindlewood sends monthly accounts to Kestrel Row; Kestrel Row reports once a year on its fund and conflicts, and within ten working days if it invests in a competitor.
payload.pt: A Brindlewood envia contas mensais à Kestrel Row; a Kestrel Row informa uma vez por ano sobre o seu fundo e os seus conflitos de interesses, e no prazo de dez dias úteis se investir num concorrente.
payload.note: Plain English and plain Portuguese (Portugal). Where they differ from the clause, the plain version states the intent.

payload.en: If the board and holders of 60% of all shares agree to sell the company, everyone sells on the same terms.
payload.pt: Se o conselho e os titulares de 60% de todas as ações aceitarem vender a empresa, todos vendem nas mesmas condições.
payload.note: Plain English and plain Portuguese (Portugal). Where they differ from the clause, the plain version states the intent.

payload.en: Every clause has a plain version in English and Portuguese; if they differ, the plain version says what was meant.
payload.pt: Cada cláusula tem uma versão em linguagem simples, em inglês e em português; se forem diferentes, a versão simples diz o que se pretendia.
payload.note: Plain English and plain Portuguese (Portugal). Where they differ from the clause, the plain version states the intent.

payload.en: Anything both lawyers confirmed in writing binds the text; a clause that contradicts it does not count until both sides sign again.
payload.pt: Tudo o que os advogados de ambos os lados confirmaram por escrito vincula o texto; uma cláusula que o contradiga não vale até que ambos os lados voltem a assinar.
payload.note: Plain English and plain Portuguese (Portugal). Where they differ from the clause, the plain version states the intent.

payload.statement: Here is our understanding: The indemnity in the warranties is capped at the amount invested, £1,200,000, not twice it.
Here is our understanding: The preference is 1x and non-participating.
Here is our understanding: The open-source licence of Wickhatch is outside every consent matter.
